Isleta Pueblo

This starting path concerns the Pueblo of Isleta in New Mexico. Its own Yonan Cultural Center, Tiwa Language Program and Cultural Committee accounts connect institutional history, learning and stewardship; it should not be conflated with Ysleta del Sur Pueblo in Texas.

01

Identity and homelands

Isleta Pueblo is a living Pueblo community and tribal government in New Mexico. Begin with the Pueblo’s own introduction.

Read the sources [1] Pueblo of Isleta

02

Historical context

A fuller history should connect the community’s own account with records of colonial rule, land, and continuity, rather than treating a mission as its origin.

Read the sources [1] Pueblo of Isleta

03

Living communities and further study

The government website provides departmental and community information. This entry is an initial source guide; a fuller cited historical synthesis remains to be developed.

Read the sources [2] Pueblo of Isleta

04

A school building becomes a cultural center

Isleta describes Yonan as a former elementary-school building that later housed the preservation department and Cultural Committee. Its account brings together archives, exhibitions, research and community knowledge sharing, with appropriate Isleta protocols guiding that work. The holdings themselves were not inspected for this guide.

Read the sources [3] Pueblo of Isleta / Department of Cultural and Historic Preservation

05

Learning Tiwa across generations

The Education Department describes teaching formats for children, youth and adults, and discusses technology as a developing tool. These statements provide a community-directed route into Isleta Tiwa learning. They do not establish present schedules, measured fluency or the completion of proposed changes.

Read the sources [4] Pueblo of Isleta / Department of Education

06

An advisory committee with a history

The Pueblo traces its Cultural Committee to 1996, when elders were appointed to advise land-claim work. Its stated mission later brings language, cultural education and environmental protection together. This institutional account does not resolve the claims or authorize disclosure of traditional knowledge.

Read the sources [5] Pueblo of Isleta
